title: Hybrid shelter wind-down plan and housing refinancing
subtitle: Affordable housing refinancing limit, mobile public health outreach, and overnight warming space questions during cold weather.
overview: The committee recommended raising the maximum total encumbrance to 90% for affordable housing projects funded through the Region, where agreements allow secondary financing {{vote:m1}}. Staff said this matches federal and provincial rules and could let providers refinance to maintain and create affordable housing. During discussion, staff and the committee agreed to change wording in the policy from "may" to "shall" for the requirement that proponents certify adequate capital reserves.

The committee defeated a motion to defer a wind-down plan for the 1001 Erb's Road hybrid shelter pending staff reports {{vote:m2}}. It also defeated a notice of motion directing staff to plan for relocating the shelter and its residents by April 2025 {{vote:m3}}. The shelter operates under a two-year pilot, and supporters said planning was needed because of a wastewater limit. Opponents said it was too early and would divert staff. Staff said the shelter will be addressed in the plan to end chronic homelessness expected in April.

The committee also received a report on mobile public health outreach clinical services, which Public Health will continue and expand. Staff answered questions on overnight warming spaces during cold weather.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended setting the total encumbrance at 90% for Region-funded affordable housing projects whose agreements permit secondary financing, and authorizing staff to execute refinancing agreements.

decisions.item: Deferral of Erb's Road shelter motion
decisions.detail: The committee defeated a motion to defer the shelter motion until staff reported, in consultation with Wilmot staff, on wastewater matters.

decisions.item: Erb's Road shelter wind-down and relocation plan
decisions.detail: The committee defeated a notice of motion directing staff to prepare a wind-down plan relocating the 1001 Erb's Road shelter and its residents by April 2025, with a report in spring 2024.

debate: On refinancing, one councillor worried that allowing 10% remaining equity raised financial risk and weakened the Region's security. Staff acknowledged some risk but said it was balanced by the chance to create more affordable housing, and that the Region holds no credit position with providers.

Supporters of the shelter motion said a building code limit on the temporary wastewater solution means a plan is needed now, either to connect to a sanitary service or to relocate, so residents are not left without options in two years.

Opponents said the motion was premature eight months into a two-year pilot, would divert staff from the plan to end chronic homelessness and from finding a second hybrid shelter, and could unsettle residents who had found stability.

Staff said the shelter is part of the interim housing plan and a wind-down would be handled compassionately, but not 14 months out. A commissioner said a temporary sanitary connection to a nearby building could be explored.

On warming spaces, staff said daytime warming spaces exist and shelters expand capacity in extreme weather, but an overnight warming space would need staffing and a physical location, much like a new shelter.
